styles.casual: Style: casual chat (Slack, Messages). Light cleanup only. Keep contractions. Don't add sign-offs.
styles.email: Style: email. Full sentences and paragraph breaks. No bullet formatting unless dictated.
styles.document: Style: document. Standard cleanup. Preserve dictated headings and numbered lists.
styles.prompt: Style: a prompt to an AI assistant. Light cleanup only. Keep technical terms and file names exactly.

paragraphs.title: Long email, several corrections, product names
paragraphs.raw: Hey Tom, so I wanted to follow up on our conversation about rolling out AI tools to the litigation team. Um, we've been piloting Claude for about, uh, six weeks now, mostly Opus for drafting and Claude Code for some of the document review scripts. The results have been really, really strong. Uh, the associates are saving maybe five to six hours a week, no, actually closer to eight hours a week on first drafts. We also looked at ChatGPT, but, um, the data retention terms didn't work for privileged material. Scratch that, the retention terms were fine, it was the admin controls that didn't work for us. Cowork has been useful for the paralegals too, especially for, you know, organizing exhibits. New paragraph. My recommendation is that we expand the pilot to the full team in January, with a, uh, a training session in the first week and a check-in at the end of the quarter. Let me know if you want me to put together a budget, I think it'd be somewhere around, um, forty thousand for the year.
paragraphs.reference:
Hey Tom,

I wanted to follow up on our conversation about rolling out AI tools to the litigation team. We've been piloting Claude for about six weeks now, mostly Opus for drafting and Claude Code for some of the document review scripts. The results have been really strong. The associates are saving closer to eight hours a week on first drafts. We also looked at ChatGPT. The retention terms were fine, it was the admin controls that didn't work for us. Cowork has been useful for the paralegals too, especially for organizing exhibits.

My recommendation is that we expand the pilot to the full team in January, with a training session in the first week and a check-in at the end of the quarter. Let me know if you want me to put together a budget. I think it'd be somewhere around $40,000 for the year.
